video_metadata.working_title: CALIFORNIA 1975 Cold Case Solved After 43 Years — Justice for the Golden State Killer's Victims
video_metadata.topic_one_sentence: From 1975 to 1986 an unknown offender known as the Visalia Ransacker, the East Area Rapist and the Original Night Stalker murdered 13 people and assaulted dozens more across California; in April 2018 crime-scene DNA, a public genealogy database and a small team of investigators and a genealogist finally named former police officer Joseph James DeAngelo, who pleaded guilty in June 2020 and was sentenced to life without parole in August 2020.
video_metadata.primary_emotion_to_evoke: Grief turned into dignified, stubborn hope: the victims and the people who refused to forget them outlasted the man who thought he had vanished.
video_metadata.research_method_note: Research done on 2026-10-09. Direct page fetching was blocked by the network proxy in this environment (WebFetch DNS/403 errors), so every fact below was gathered from web-search result summaries of the listed pages (24 queries before the shared search budget ran out). Every fact is tied to the source(s) whose summary contained it. Items not confirmed in-session are flagged in notes_and_gaps and are NOT used in the script.

protagonist._instructions: The main character of your story - can be hero, villain, or antihero. Fill with verified facts only.
protagonist.full_name: Joseph James DeAngelo (also written Joseph DeAngelo Jr. in the Contra Costa DA release [1])
protagonist.age_at_time_of_events: 29 at the Snelling murder (Sept 1975), 32 at the Maggiore murders (Feb 1978), 40 at the Cruz murder (May 1986) — derived from birth date Nov 8, 1945 [56][64]; 72 at arrest (April 2018) [53][55]; 74 at plea and sentencing (2020) [5][59]; 80 as of 2026 [3]
protagonist.occupation_or_status: U.S. Navy veteran of the Vietnam era [56][57]; police officer in Exeter, CA from 1973 (end date reported as 1975 or 1976) [57][59][64]; police officer in Auburn, CA 1976–1979, fired in August 1979 after being caught shoplifting a hammer and a can of dog repellent, convicted of the theft and fined $100 [53][58][64]; later a mechanic, retired at time of arrest [55]. Convicted: pleaded guilty June 29, 2020 to 13 counts of first-degree murder and 13 counts of kidnapping for robbery [7]; sentenced Aug 21, 2020 to 11 consecutive terms of life without parole plus an additional life term plus eight years [5].
protagonist.location: Lived in Citrus Heights, Sacramento County, at the time of arrest [53][55]; now in the Protective Housing Unit at California State Prison, Corcoran (A&E, 2026) [3]
protagonist.physical_description: At the 2020 hearings he appeared in a wheelchair, and at sentencing rose from it and removed his mask to address the court [5][6].
protagonist.background_brief: Born November 8, 1945 in Bath, New York [56][57]. Served in the Navy during the Vietnam War; one account says as a damage control man aboard the USS Canberra (single-source) [56]. The Exeter Sun of Aug 22, 1973 reported him as a new Exeter officer and Vietnam veteran from Bath, NY [57]. Exeter is about 12 miles from Visalia, where the Ransacker burglaries and the Snelling murder occurred [11]. Fired by Auburn PD in 1979 for shoplifting [53][58]. Former Auburn chief described him as an average cop [58].
protagonist.psychological_profile: Only documented statements are used. Prosecutor Thien Ho said at the plea hearing that DeAngelo, alone in an interrogation room after arrest, said 'I did all that', spoke of a figure called 'Jerry' he had 'pushed out', said he had 'destroyed all their lives' and that he now had to pay the price [9][8]. Ho said DeAngelo had 'feigned feeble incoherence' to detectives and in 1979 faked a heart attack when caught shoplifting, later admitting he had 'just pretended to act crazy' [10]. No motive or diagnosis is asserted in the script.
protagonist.mundane_humanizing_detail: Retired mechanic in a Sacramento suburb; on April 18, 2018 investigators swabbed his car door handle while he was shopping inside a Hobby Lobby in Roseville [47][49].
protagonist.nickname_or_alias_if_any: Visalia Ransacker; East Area Rapist (EAR); Original Night Stalker (ONS); Golden State Killer (name coined by Michelle McNamara, Los Angeles Magazine, March 2013) [36][37][64]

victims_or_targets._instructions: People affected by the protagonist's actions. Include 3-5 key figures minimum.

individuals.name: Claude Snelling
individuals.role_or_profession: Journalism professor, College of the Sequoias, Visalia; age 45
individuals.connection_to_protagonist: Murdered Sept 11, 1975 (early hours) while confronting a masked gunman who was taking his daughter from the home
individuals.specific_impact_suffered: Shot twice; died on the way to the hospital [11][12]
individuals.humanizing_detail: Daughter described him as a man of faith who loved his family more than anything and lived life to the fullest [12]; he had earlier caught a prowler peering through her window and chased him [12]

individuals.name: Elizabeth Hupp (née Snelling)
individuals.role_or_profession: Claude Snelling's daughter; teenager in 1975 (age reported as 16 or 17 — disputed) [11][12]
individuals.connection_to_protagonist: Survivor of the attempted abduction; DeAngelo admitted the attempted kidnapping in 2020 [12]
individuals.specific_impact_suffered: Kicked in the head and face; years of guilt; fear as the only living witness [12]
individuals.humanizing_detail: Realised only after becoming a parent that nothing could have stopped her father from trying to save her [12]
individuals.any_quotes_from_them: 'It wasn't until I became a parent myself that I realized there was nothing I could have said that would have kept my dad from trying to save me.' / 'He would have been a wonderful grandpa.' [12]

individuals.name: Brian Maggiore
individuals.role_or_profession: U.S. Air Force sergeant, age 21; one account: administrative specialist at Mather Air Force Base [13][14][15]
individuals.connection_to_protagonist: Murdered Feb 2, 1978 in Rancho Cordova while walking the dog with his wife; these two murders were the counts on which DeAngelo was first arrested in 2018 [13][53]

individuals.name: Katie Maggiore
individuals.role_or_profession: Age 20 (CBS gives reverse ages; one source 20 and 22) [14][15][16]
individuals.specific_impact_suffered: Shot; police believe the couple were shot in a neighbour's backyard while fleeing (Sacramento Bee via Oxygen) [14]
individuals.humanizing_detail: Her brother Ken Smith said 'Katie and Brian were special, and we all loved them so much.' [16][17]

individuals.name: Dr. Robert Offerman and Debra Alexandria Manning
individuals.connection_to_protagonist: Murdered Dec 30, 1979 in a condominium near Goleta, Santa Barbara County [29][30][68]

individuals.name: Lyman Smith and Charlene Smith
individuals.role_or_profession: Lyman, 43, former deputy district attorney; Charlene, 33 [19][21]
individuals.connection_to_protagonist: Murdered in their Ventura home on March 13, 1980 (some sources give March 16, likely the discovery date — disputed) [19][21]
individuals.specific_impact_suffered: Bludgeoned to death; bodies found by a 12-year-old boy, Jennifer Carole's younger brother [19][21][22]. The tissue DNA collected April 23, 2018 matched semen from Charlene Smith's case [48].
individuals.humanizing_detail: Lyman's daughter Jennifer Carole was 18 at the time and wrote that it was as if 'a bomb went off in our young lives' [19]

individuals.name: Keith Harrington and Patrice (Patty) Harrington
individuals.role_or_profession: Keith, 24, fourth-year medical student; Patrice, nurse, age reported as 27 or 28 (disputed) [23][24][25]
individuals.connection_to_protagonist: Murdered Aug 19, 1980 at home in Niguel Shores, a gated community then in unincorporated Orange County, now Dana Point [25]
individuals.specific_impact_suffered: Bludgeoned to death; married only three months [25]
individuals.humanizing_detail: Keith's brother Bruce Harrington spent years and his own money backing California's DNA database law, Proposition 69 [23][24]

individuals.name: Manuela Witthuhn
individuals.role_or_profession: Age 28; bank teller per City of Irvine (Oxygen says loan officer) [26][14]
individuals.connection_to_protagonist: Murdered at home in Irvine between 11 p.m. Feb 5 and 2 a.m. Feb 6, 1981 [26][27]
individuals.specific_impact_suffered: Died of skull fractures from a beating; found by her parents [27][14]
individuals.humanizing_detail: Her husband David was in hospital with a stomach virus; after visiting him she went home, and he phoned to make sure she had arrived safely — the last time he spoke to her [27][28]

individuals.name: Cheri Domingo and Gregory Sanchez
individuals.connection_to_protagonist: Murdered July 27, 1981 in a house near Goleta where Cheri was house-sitting (one CBS report: July 26) [29][30]
individuals.specific_impact_suffered: Both beaten; Sanchez had also been shot [29][30]
individuals.humanizing_detail: Cheri's daughter Debbi Domingo McMullan was 15 at the time [MINOR then] [29]

individuals.name: Janelle Lisa Cruz
individuals.connection_to_protagonist: Last known murder victim; killed in her Irvine home in early May 1986 (May 4 or 5 — disputed) while her family was on vacation in Mexico [35][22]
individuals.humanizing_detail: Her sister Michelle, one year younger, spent years raising awareness of the case [31][35]

collective_victims_if_applicable.group_description: Survivors of home-invasion rapes and burglaries in the Sacramento area, the San Joaquin Valley, the Bay Area and Southern California, plus the families of 13 murder victims
collective_victims_if_applicable.total_number_affected: DeAngelo admitted crimes against 87 individual victims at 53 separate crime scenes (Contra Costa DA via A&E) [1][3]. Counts of uncharged admissions are reported differently: 161 uncharged offenses (State Hornet) vs up to 62 uncharged rapes (Fox) — disputed [7][8].
collective_victims_if_applicable.range_of_impacts: 13 murders; dozens of rapes too old to prosecute because of the statute of limitations; years of fear ('After 42 years I still look over my shoulder' — survivor statement headline, TheWrap) [5][61]

supporting_characters._instructions: Investigators, accomplices, witnesses, family members - anyone who plays a significant role.

characters.name: Michelle McNamara
characters.role_in_story: True-crime writer; coined 'Golden State Killer' in 'In the Footsteps of a Killer', Los Angeles Magazine, March 2013 [36][37]
characters.key_actions_they_took: Spent years researching; signed a book contract after the article; died in her sleep April 21, 2016, age 46 (drugs plus undiagnosed heart condition) [37]; book 'I'll Be Gone in the Dark' completed by Billy Jensen and Paul Haynes from her notes and 3,500+ computer files, published Feb 27, 2018, reached No. 1 on the NYT nonfiction list, two months before the arrest [38]
characters.notable_quotes: None used (her book's text not quoted)

characters.name: Patton Oswalt
characters.key_actions_they_took: Enlisted Jensen and Haynes to finish the book [38]; reacted publicly to arrest, plea and sentencing [39][40][41]
characters.notable_quotes: 'You did it, Michelle.' (2018) [39]; 'She kept coming at him.' [39]; 'The most important people at the #GoldenStateKiller hearing today are the survivors.' (June 2020) [41]; 'The insect gets none of my headspace today.' (Aug 2020) [40]

characters.name: Paul Holes
characters.role_in_story: Forensic investigator who worked the case for decades [42][43]
characters.key_actions_they_took: Brought genealogist Barbara Rae-Venter into the case (reported as March 2017 — timing single-sourced) [43]; the day before he retired, drove alone to DeAngelo's house and debated knocking on the door to ask for a DNA sample, but stayed in the car [50][51]; memoir 'Unmasked: My Life Solving America's Cold Cases' (2022) [50]
characters.notable_quotes: 'Fortunately I didn't go up to the door.' [50]

characters.name: Barbara Rae-Venter
characters.role_in_story: Genetic genealogist; book 'I Know Who You Are: How an Amateur DNA Sleuth Unmasked the Golden State Killer and Changed Crime Fighting Forever' (2023) [44]
characters.key_actions_they_took: Drafted a suspect profile from old newspaper articles suggesting law enforcement or military experience; worked from more than 1,000 'genetic cousins' returned by GEDmatch; built family trees with traditional genealogy [42][43]

characters.name: Anne Marie Schubert
characters.key_actions_they_took: Announced the arrest April 25, 2018 (National DNA Day) [52]
characters.notable_quotes: 'We knew we were looking for a needle in a haystack, but we also knew that needle was there.' / 'We found the needle in the haystack, and it was right here in Sacramento.' [52][53]

characters.name: Thien Ho
characters.key_actions_they_took: Presented facts at the June 29, 2020 plea hearing including DeAngelo's interrogation-room monologue [9][10]; read Loretta Maggiore's statement [18]

characters.name: Judge Michael Bowman
characters.notable_quotes: 'The defendant deserves no mercy.' [5]; without the persistence of survivors, families, citizen detectives and law enforcement, DeAngelo 'may have escaped earthly justice altogether.' [4]

characters.name: Tim Ward
characters.key_actions_they_took: Charged the Snelling murder in August 2018, calling Snelling believed to be the first murder victim [11]

characters.name: Bruce Harrington
characters.key_actions_they_took: Researched, funded and shaped Proposition 69 (2004), requiring DNA samples from all felony arrestees; passed with more than 62% [23][24]
characters.notable_quotes: Arrest would 'bring closure to the anguish that we all suffered for the last 40-odd years.' [23]

characters.name: Ken Smith
characters.notable_quotes: 'You are not worth any more of my family's time.' / 'You can't hurt anybody again.' / 'Closure means there is an end, but nothing changes. You can't bring Katie and Brian back.' [16][17]

characters.name: Karen Smith
characters.notable_quotes: 'They loved life and everybody loved them in the 18 months they were married.' / 'The only thing I'm happy for is that I got to live long enough to see this happen.' [16]

characters.name: Loretta Maggiore
characters.key_actions_they_took: One-sentence statement read in court by prosecutor Thien Ho: she had nothing good to say about DeAngelo, so she would say nothing at all to him (paraphrase as reported) [16][18]

characters.name: Jennifer Carole
characters.role_in_story: Daughter of Lyman Smith; writer and advocate
characters.key_actions_they_took: Spoke publicly and gave a victim impact statement; criticised the plea outcome [19][20][21]
characters.notable_quotes: 'From the outside, he looks particularly ordinary and yet we know on the inside there's a monster there.' [21][22]; criticised his 'friction-free' existence since arrest [20]

characters.name: Michelle Cruz
characters.role_in_story: Janelle Cruz's sister, one year younger [31][35]
characters.key_actions_they_took: Raised awareness for years; victim impact statement Aug 20, 2020 [28][32]
characters.notable_quotes: Murder 'completely changed my world, my life, my identity' [31]; 'I can finally breathe again' (headline quote, 2018) [31]; 'cried and cried for hours' after the arrest [28]; 'Now my time will no longer [be] concentrated on who killed my sister but rather on finding happiness and enjoyment, which I had lost because of Joseph DeAngelo 34 years ago' [32]; 'Why did he stop after Jeanelle?' (CBS Sacramento, date unclear) [33]

characters.name: Diane Stein
characters.key_actions_they_took: Spoke to First Coast News after the sentence [34]
characters.notable_quotes: 'She can rest in peace now' (headline quote) [34]

characters.name: Debbi Domingo McMullan
characters.key_actions_they_took: Family member of victims (statement content not verified in-session)

cold_open_material._instructions: The most dramatic moment of your story - this will be your hook.

the_moment.what_is_happening: Air Force sergeant Brian Maggiore, 21, and his wife Katie, 20, walk their dog through their neighbourhood
the_moment.what_makes_it_shocking: They are chased and shot; the killer vanishes for 40 years
the_moment.ironic_twist: The man later convicted had worn a police badge; his arrest warrant in 2018 was for these two murders

cold_open_material.central_mystery_question: How did one man commit 13 murders across California and live quietly in a Sacramento suburb for 32 years after the last one — and who refused to let him stay hidden?

the_method._instructions: How did the protagonist do what they did? Technical details that can be explained to a general audience.
step_by_step_explanation: Crime-scene DNA preserved from decades-old cases
Profile converted to a format a consumer genealogy site can read and uploaded to GEDmatch (and FamilyTreeDNA) [42][45]
Database returns distant relatives: more than 1,000 'genetic cousins' [42]
Genealogist works backwards to the most recent common ancestor of matched cousins using public records [46]
Builds the full descendant tree forward and filters by age, sex, location [46]
Narrowed to a handful of men; eye-color prediction used (ResearchGate; single-source detail) [46]
Surveillance and discarded DNA: car door handle (April 18) and tissue in trash (April 23) produce a standard STR profile matching CODIS crime-scene profiles [46][47][48]
the_method.why_it_worked: Distant relatives of the offender had voluntarily uploaded DNA to a public database; crime-scene samples had been preserved since the 1970s–80s [45][48]

technical_terms_to_explain.simple_explanation: The law-enforcement DNA database; only finds a person already in it
A person who shares a stretch of DNA with you because of a shared ancestor
Traces left on objects a person touches or throws away, collected without a warrant
The standard forensic DNA 'fingerprint' used for a confirming match

systemic_failure._instructions: What institution, system, or authority failed to prevent this?
systemic_failure.institution_that_failed: Fragmented local law enforcement across multiple counties; 1970s–80s forensic limits
systemic_failure.why_they_failed: Crimes spread over many jurisdictions and names; no DNA technology before the late 1980s; offender not in any database
specific_incompetence_examples: A police officer fired in 1979 for shoplifting a hammer and dog repellent was never connected to the series at the time [53][58]
Thousands of tips over the years; DeAngelo's name not on authorities' radar until the week before arrest (Schubert) [53]
The Snelling bullets matched a gun stolen in a Visalia burglary, but the killer was not identified for 43 years [11]
Uncharged rapes could no longer be prosecuted because of the statute of limitations [5]
systemic_failure.ironic_details_about_the_failure: He worked as a police officer in Exeter, about 12 miles from Visalia, during the Ransacker period [11]

the_investigation.investigating_agency: Multi-agency task force including Sacramento County DA's Office and Sheriff's Department, FBI, Contra Costa County, Ventura, Orange, Santa Barbara and Tulare counties [1][52][53]
the_investigation.initial_wrong_assumptions: Crimes treated as separate series under different names until DNA linked them [37]
the_investigation.key_breakthrough: Genetic genealogy via GEDmatch in early 2018 [45]
the_investigation.the_fatal_mistake: Touching his own car door and throwing a tissue away [47][48]
the_investigation.how_long_until_caught: About 43 years after the first murder (1975–2018); 40 years after the Maggiore murders; 32 years after the last

the_confrontation._instructions: The arrest, raid, or climactic moment when everything collapses.
the_confrontation.date_and_time: April 24, 2018 (booked around 2 a.m. April 25 per one report) [52][53]
the_confrontation.scene_description: Arrested at home by Sacramento authorities on two counts of murder [53]
the_confrontation.protagonist_reaction: Alone in the interview room he said 'I did all that' and spoke of 'Jerry' (as recounted by prosecutor Thien Ho) [9]
the_confrontation.ironic_or_absurd_details: Arrest announced on National DNA Day [52]

charges_filed: 13 counts of first-degree murder (Sacramento, Ventura, Orange, Santa Barbara, Tulare counties) [7][11][30]
legal_resolution.notable_court_testimony: Prosecutors recounted the crimes at the plea; DeAngelo repeatedly said 'guilty' and 'I admit' [8]

victim_impact_statements.key_quote: 'He would have been a wonderful grandpa.'
'The only thing I'm happy for is that I got to live long enough to see this happen.'
'…finding happiness and enjoyment, which I had lost because of Joseph DeAngelo 34 years ago'

legal_resolution.sentence_received: 11 consecutive life terms without the possibility of parole, plus an additional life term, plus eight years (AP) [5]; Contra Costa DA: 11 consecutive LWOP for 13 murders plus an additional consecutive life term for the 13 kidnappings [2]
legal_resolution.protagonist_statement_in_court: 'I've listened to all your statements. Each one of them. And I'm truly sorry to everyone I've hurt.' (ABC; AP wording: 'truly sorry for everyone I've hurt') [6][5]
legal_resolution.current_status: Serving life without parole; held in the Protective Housing Unit at California State Prison, Corcoran; age 80 (A&E, 2026). No appeals, new charges or sentence changes found in 2023–2026 coverage [3]. Plea waived the death penalty [3][4].
